title: [D4 Rendering] Bounded rendering with visible truncation
summary: The triage rendering is bounded. `helena.rendering.RenderingBudget` is a number of characters read from `config/rendering.toml` by `rendering.budget()` — required, no default anywhere in the code — and `helena.rendering.v1.render(projection, attributes, budget)` turns it into a deterministic selection over lines: two sections and every source header are never dropped, what is kept is a prefix of the projection's neutral order, the budget is shared max-min fair between the three record-carrying sections, and a section that dropped a record carries a `helena.contracts.v1.Truncation` AND opens with a `truncated kept=N total=N dropped=N` line. `scripts/measure_rendering.py` (`make rendering-size`) is the instrument the number came from, and `docs/decisions/0019-the-rendering-size-budget.md` records the four rules, the measurement and what is still open.
assumption_validated: That the rendering can be bounded without any section shrinking invisibly, and that the busy-host size the PRD calls unmeasured can be measured rather than assumed. Both positive, and the measurement changed the answer. Over the whole of `data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl` — 62 real flow records, one managed Windows 10 endpoint, 130.8 s, two windows — the busier window holds **122 entity rows** (55 domain, 31 address, 4 fingerprint, 32 url) and renders to **12 115 characters**; the quieter holds 10 and renders to 1 770. That is 2.4x the only number this project had before (ADR-0018's 4 964 for the ten-record layer-coverage capture, from the same host), so a budget argued from the earlier figure would have been about half of what a real quiet endpoint needs. A second result worth recording as negative: 32 of the 122 rows are `url` entities that rendering v1 does not carry, so the rendering is materially smaller than the context before any budget applies — the enrichment gap ADR-0018 escalated is also a sizing distortion. And one property is NOT demonstrated: no model has read one of these renderings, so whether 25 000 characters is a comfortable input for a small fast model on the high-volume path is unmeasured, and the value is recorded as a candidate rather than a decision.
makes_buildable: Task 30/31 have everything the triage runner needs and one obligation. The call is `rendering.budget()`, then `rendering.version('v1').render(projection, attributes, budget)`; the request already carries the result, because `AgentRequest.rendering` is the `Rendering` and `Rendering.truncations` is what reads it. The obligation: `contracts.check_exchange` refuses an outcome carrying no `truncated` gap when the rendering truncated, and this is the first increment that can actually produce one — `tests/test_rendering.py::test_the_truncation_reaches_the_request_and_forces_a_gap` shows the exact shape of the gap the runner has to emit. D5 has the two things it must store: `Truncation.section/kept/total` per section, and a count of them per section that would make a wrong budget observable the way `helena_signal_retention_rejections` makes a wrong retention horizon observable.

verification.detail: 982 passed (963 before this task; 19 new). Every rendering test executes against a throwaway RisingWave 3.0.3 holding a real capture and a real ThreatFox extract. The bounding test is a sweep: one real context rendered at every budget from 'everything fits' down to 'nothing does' (13-character steps, ~390 renderings), asserting at each step that the rendering is inside its budget, that every section's record-line count is either the projection's total or exactly its `Truncation.kept`, and that a section which kept everything carries no record. Three mutation checks were run and each was caught: dropping the `Truncation` from a shrunken section (3 tests fail), making the source header lines droppable (2 fail), and computing `evidence_ids` over the projection instead of the kept lines (1 fails, the citation one). `scripts/measure_rendering.py` was run against the real engine at the configured budget and at 4 000, and `uv lock --check` plus `compileall` pass.

escalations.detail: A second configuration FILE, `config/rendering.toml`, read by `helena.rendering.budget()`. Recorded because `concept/instruction.md` §3 and `prds/CONTEXT.md` §6 make 'a second store of any kind, including a cache, a queue or a file' an escalation. Judged not to be a store and built anyway, on exactly the grounds task 27 recorded for `config/hosts.toml` and which the operator did not object to: nothing is written to it, nothing durable is recovered from it, it holds no evidence, and it is read once at startup. The positive reason is stronger here than there — `concept/07` says budget values are POLICY and not constants in a branch, so a number in a Python module would break an invariant, and the alternative (a new required environment variable through `helena.config.Settings`) would touch every test module's environment dict and `.env` for one value. If the operator disagrees, the file is the only thing to move: `budget(path)` already takes the path.

`helena.rendering.v1.render` gained a third required parameter and `RenderingVersion.render` is now `(projection, host_attributes, budget)`. Recorded because it changes a versioned module's signature. It is not a change to the AGENT contract — nothing in `helena.contracts` moved, and `Truncation` was already there, unused, waiting for exactly this. `v1` was extended rather than superseded by a `v2` because nothing has recorded `rendering_version = "v1"` — there is no assessment table yet (task 26 deferred it to D5), so no stored row is pinned to the unbounded shape, and boundedness is part of what `concept/04` says a rendering IS rather than a change to what one means. The moment D5 writes a row, `v1.py` is frozen and a change to the selection is a `v2`. ADR-0019 §6 records this.

deferred: STORING A TRUNCATION. There is no assessment table (task 26 deferred it to D5), so a `Truncation` reaches an `AgentRequest` in memory and no further. `concept/instruction.md` §7's 'versions recorded on every citable row' and 'every new failure path is typed, stored and countable' stay open for the agent layer exactly as tasks 26, 27 and 28 left them — what is countable here is countable in a rendering object, not in a row. The thing D5 should build is a truncation count per section, which is what would make a wrong budget observable rather than argued.

THE 'CONTRIBUTING-EVENTS LIST' THE TASK NAMES. It does not exist in this repository — `concept/08-open-questions.md` line 44 is the only mention anywhere, and it names an artifact of the finding/assessment output that D5 has not built. The unbounded list that DOES exist in D4 is the per-entity record list of the three enriched sections, and that is what was bounded. Recorded rather than quietly re-scoped, per `concept/instruction.md` §4: the task's step was written before the rendering had a shape.

A TOKEN BUDGET. Characters, not tokens, and the conversion is deliberately not written down anywhere. Counting tokens needs a tokenizer per model and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint does not publish its vocabulary; adding one is a runtime dependency for a number that would be wrong for the next model. Characters bound the token count from above for every tokenizer there is but are not proportional to it — this rendering is unusually token-hostile text — so a ratio would be a guess. ADR-0019 §2.

A SECOND BUDGET KNOB. One number, not a per-section cap, not a record cap, not a per-source paragraph allowance. `SourceDescriptor.caveat` — 600 characters for `sslbl-ja3`, real and relevant, deferred by ADR-0018 §9 as 'a budget decision that belongs with the budget' — stays deferred: it is a decision about what an agent may see, and it wants a measurement saying the single knob is wrong before it gets a second one.

A PROMPT BUDGET. The budget covers the five section bodies and not the prompt around them. The prompt is task 30/31's, it is not attacker-influenced, and a budget covering both would make a rendering shrink because somebody reworded an instruction.

MAKING A DROPPED HIT VISIBLE AS SOMETHING OTHER THAN A COUNT. A truncated section says how many records it dropped and not what was in them. Saying 'and 3 of the dropped records carried a malicious claim' would be a hits-aware summary of the negative space and is the same decision as hits-first selection, one level down; it is also the composition rule's job (task 32), not a formatter's.
lessons: THE FLOW FIXTURE IS 122 ENTITY ROWS AND 12 115 CHARACTERS IN ITS BUSIER WINDOW, not the 4 964 ADR-0018 measured. Same host, same file: 0018 measured the ten-record layer-coverage extract and this is the whole 62-record sample. Any later sizing argument should start from 122/12 115, and `make rendering-size` re-measures it for any capture. 32 of the 122 rows are `url` entities that rendering v1 does not carry, so the rendered size is not a proxy for the context size.

TO MEASURE OR RENDER A COMMITTED FIXTURE, SHIFT `ts` BY A WHOLE NUMBER OF WINDOWS — NEVER INTO ONE WINDOW. Every fixture here is dated 2024-06-01 and the retention boundary shows none of it, so tests/scripts re-stamp. `tests/test_rendering.py::live` collapses the capture into a single window on purpose, but doing that to the flow sample destroys the fact that it CROSSES a boundary and is two contexts: you would then measure a 132-row host that does not exist. Shifting by `k * 300 s` keeps the partition identical and both windows land inside retention.

`RenderedSection.evidence_ids` MUST BE COMPUTED OVER THE KEPT LINES, NEVER OVER THE PROJECTION. `check_exchange` resolves a result's citations against that list, so a section advertising an identifier it dropped lets a model cite evidence it was never shown and the contract ACCEPTS it. That is the one way a truncation bug becomes a false audit trail rather than a short rendering. The shape that prevents it: the evidence ids travel on the same object as the line, so dropping the line drops them.

A TRUNCATION MARKER'S COST IS CIRCULAR IF YOU CHARGE IT PER TRUNCATED SECTION — the marker's length depends on the kept count and the kept count depends on the marker's length. The way out is two paths: check whether the whole rendering fits first (the common case, and it pays nothing), and in the slow path reserve one marker for EVERY record-carrying section before allocating. A section that then turns out to fit has paid for a marker it does not use, which leaves the rendering slightly under budget — the safe direction.

ALLOCATE A SHARED BUDGET MAX-MIN FAIR, NOT SEQUENTIALLY. 'Each section in order takes what it needs' starves the last one: a host that contacted six hundred domains would render no TLS parameters at all. Max-min is ~15 lines (give every section that wants less than an equal share all of it, re-divide the rest, repeat) and is order-independent; the indivisible remainder goes to the earliest section in `contract.SECTIONS` so the split is a function of the inputs and not of dict order.

A NEUTRAL PREFIX CAN DROP A MALICIOUS HIT, AND THAT IS NOT A LOST ALERT. The objection to non-hits-first selection has a concept-level answer worth reusing: `concept/04`'s second escalation input is deterministic and independent — a Tier A or high-confidence Tier B classification escalates REGARDLESS of the triage verdict — and it reads the store, not the rendering. The rendering is what a model reasons over; it is not the alerting path. A selection rule that tried to make it one would be prejudging the composition rule inside a formatter.

THE SOURCE HEADER IS THE LINE A BUDGET MUST NOT TOUCH, and it is the one a record-counting truncation record would hide. `Truncation.kept/total` count records; a header is not a record, so dropping one is invisible in the record AND collapses `missing`/`failed` into 'nothing known' — the exact thing `concept/instruction.md` §2 forbids 'including in whatever is rendered to an agent'. A budget too small for the headers is a `RenderingError`, not a smaller rendering.
failed_approaches: task 29: Charging the truncation marker line only to the sections that actually truncate. It does not terminate as written: the marker text carries the kept count, so its length depends on the decision it is an input to. Two other dead ends around it — computing the kept count first and then re-deriving it with the marker reserved (a section can flip out of truncation and back), and using a fixed-width marker (either wrong for four-digit counts or wasteful for one-digit ones). What works is the fast path plus a per-section reserve sized at `_marker(total, total)`.

task 29: Putting the budget in `helena.config.Settings` as a required environment variable. It is the obvious home and it is the wrong one here: every test module carries its own `ENVIRONMENT` dict and `.env` would need the value too, so one number would ripple through ~20 files, and a rendering budget is deployment policy of the same kind as the host inventory rather than an endpoint or a credential. `config/rendering.toml` beside `config/hosts.toml` costs one escalation and nothing else.

task 29: Setting the budget to 24 000 on the reasoning 'double the measured 12 115'. It is not — 2 x 12 115 is 24 230 — and the test that asserts the CRITERION (`busiest[1] * 2 <= rendering.budget().characters`) caught it where a test asserting the number would have passed. The value is 25 000. Worth repeating the shape rather than the arithmetic: assert the property the number was chosen for, not the number.

task 29: Writing the 'no [budget] table' test case as a file containing `characters = 24000` at the top level. That hits the earlier 'top-level keys nothing reads' arm, so the test proved a different refusal than it claimed to. An empty (comment-only) file is the case that reaches it.
next_session_should_know: The rendering is bounded and the call signature changed: `v1.render(projection, attributes, budget)`, with the budget from `rendering.budget()` reading `config/rendering.toml` (25 000 characters). There is no default and `render` refuses a plain int, so a caller cannot forget it. FOUR THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE MOMENT YOU BUILD A REQUEST FROM A TRUNCATED RENDERING YOU OWE A GAP. `check_exchange` refuses an outcome with no `truncated` gap when `request.rendering.truncations` is non-empty — so the triage runner must inspect that and emit `contract.Gap(kind=contract.TRUNCATED, detail=...)` on the result. `tests/test_rendering.py::test_the_truncation_reaches_the_request_and_forces_a_gap` is the worked example, including the exact `model_copy` shape. (2) THE BUDGET IS A CANDIDATE, NOT A DECISION, and the thing that would settle it is a busy host observed through truncation counts — which needs the assessment table D5 has not built. Do not treat 25 000 as validated: no model has read one of these renderings, so its comfort for a small fast model is unmeasured, and `concept/08` still lists the numeric budget values as open. (3) IF YOU CHANGE ANYTHING THE RENDERING EMITS, `tests/test_rendering.py::test_the_whole_flow_sample_renders_to_the_size_the_notes_record` will fail with an exact character count — that is deliberate, and the fix is to re-run `make rendering-size` and update `config/rendering.toml` and ADR-0019 together, not to relax the assertion. (4) `helena/rendering/` may still hold only `__init__.py` and `vN.py`; the budget VALUE OBJECT and its loader are machinery and live in `__init__.py`, the SELECTION is format-specific and lives in `v1.py`. One correction landed in this commit: ADR-0018 §9's last bullet said 'no section produced here carries one' of `Truncation`, which this task made false, so it now carries a `Superseded by 0019` note and the corrected fixture measurement. Also unchanged and still true from task 28: `rendering.RenderingStore(...).project(context_id)` raises `ContextOutsideRetention` for a context outside the boundary, so every engine test here re-stamps its capture into a live window.
